The fiddle is a bowed string instrument, most often meaning the violin or the double bass, in the bowed / wheel-bowed / fiddle family of chordophones, Hornbostel-Sachs number 321.322-71. The player draws a bow across the strings, sometimes using a flatter-arched bridge and steel strings, which makes techniques such as the double shuffle (rapid alternation between neighbouring strings) easier and gives a brighter tone. It is common in traditional folk music, mostly passed on by ear, and is used for dance accompaniment; it can be played by a soloist, by one or two fiddlers with others, and it is also found in twin-fiddle traditions in Scotland, Ireland, North America and Scandinavia.
